title: Reshaping: pivot and melt
summary: Long versus wide tables: pivot_table to spread values into columns, melt to gather them back, and crosstab for counts.
hints: `units_wide`: `df.pivot_table(index="month", columns="product", values="units", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)`. The months become the index (named `month`) and the products the columns (whose axis is named `product`). Duplicate (month, product) pairs are summed.

`to_long`: `wide.reset_index()` turns `month` back into a column, then `.melt(id_vars="month", var_name="product", value_name="units")`. Finish with `.sort_values(["month", "product"]).reset_index(drop=True)`.

`region_product_counts`: `pd.crosstab(df["region"], df["product"])` counts rows per pair. `best_product_per_month`: take `units_wide(df)` and call `.idxmax(axis=1)`: for each row (month) it names the column (product) holding the maximum; `.to_dict()` gives `{month: product}`.
